questions.question: Describe the circuit in a toy of your choice in terms of its energy source, switch, device and output.
questions.expected_answer: Example: a remote-control car has a battery pack as the energy source, wires and a switch, and electric motors as devices that change electrical energy into movement of the wheels and steering. A talking doll has cells, a switch that closes when squeezed, and a speaker that gives sound. Toys use cells, never mains electricity.

questions.question: Name and describe the steps of the design process.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate: find out about the problem and existing solutions. Design: write a design brief, draw ideas and a circuit diagram, and list materials. Make: build the model safely and test the circuit as you go. Evaluate: test the finished model, check it meets the brief and decide how to improve it. Communicate: present and explain the model.

questions.question: Explain how the steady-hand game works and give two safety rules for building models with circuits.
questions.expected_answer: A bent bare wire and a loop on a handle are part of a circuit with a cell and a buzzer, with a gap between the loop and the wire. If the loop touches the wire, the gap closes, the circuit is complete and the buzzer sounds, so the loop and wire act as a switch. Safety rules: use only cells, never mains electricity; never join the terminals of a cell with a bare wire; use sharp tools carefully with an adult; remove cells when not in use.
